summary: Yu counts ℓ-adic local systems of rank n on a curve over F_q that are fixed by Frobenius, through Drinfeld's method and the Arthur–Lafforgue trace formula, and relates the count to stable Higgs bundles and to geometrically indecomposable bundles through Mellit's polynomial A_{g,n}; for degree coprime to n it does not depend on the degree. Complete (cc-442dc5): every numbered statement is an item, every missing item is routed exactly once, and twenty-seven findings are recorded. Lemma 6.3.2(b) is false for non-diagonalizable matrices (E16), Corollaries 4.2.6 and 6.1.2 need added hypotheses (E4, E15), and the rest are misprints or proof points. Not formalised.

items.name: Clifford decomposition and the twist stabilizer

The inducing class is unique up to that orbit. Fix=1 iff geometric restriction is irreducible.

items.name: Regularized family value and descent
items.statement: The sum Σ_Q c_Q(lambda)/theta_Q(lambda) extends holomorphically near 1 and defines c_M at 1. Parabolic restrictions give (L,M)-families, and restriction to X_L^G gives a well-defined (G,L)-family independent of an intermediate parabolic.

items.name: Product formula for families
items.statement: If c_M^Q is independent of Q∈P(L) for every L⊇M, then (cd)_M=Σ_L c_M^L d_L in Yu's normalization. This hypothesis is essential; the formula is not asserted for arbitrary families without the partial-value compatibility.

items.name: Root-product derivative formula
items.statement: For each root beta choose c_beta meromorphic on C*, regular at 1 with c_beta(1)=1. The products c_Q=∏_{beta∈Phi_Q} c_beta(lambda^beta∨) form a family; c_M=Σ_F ∏_{beta∈F}c_beta'(1), where F ranges over root subsets forming a basis of a_M^{G,*}.

items.name: Root-coordinate Haar integral
items.statement: For a root basis F and continuous functions on S1, the map Im X_M^G→(S1)^F has finite central kernel and pushes probability Haar measure to probability Haar measure. Consequently the product integral factors into the one-variable contour integrals with dz/(2πi).

items.name: Argument-principle integral of a family
items.statement: Assume each c_beta is meromorphic on a neighborhood of the closed unit disk and nonzero and finite on S1. For the ratio root-product family, its integrated regularized value is Σ_F∏_{beta∈F}(N(c_beta)−P(c_beta)), counting multiplicities in |z|<1. Rational L-ratios satisfy the needed extension assumption when boundary singularities are absent.

items.name: Ambient independence and central-translation vanishing
items.statement: For the root-product families, c_M^R is independent of the ambient parabolic R with a fixed Levi. If c_Q(lambda mu0)=c_Q(lambda) and all partial values have this independence, the translated regularized sum vanishes unless mu0 is central; in the central case it is mu01^−dim(a_M^G)c_M.

items.name: Generic auxiliary chamber selector
items.statement: Choose kappa in the positive chamber outside every relative-root hyperplane for every semistandard Levi. The unique Q_L with all its simple roots positive on kappa orders the Levi blocks. Merely requiring nonzero projections to a_L is insufficient.

items.name: Rankin–Selberg normalizing factors

items.name: Degree-filtered lattice cone series
items.statement: The meromorphic cone series hat1_Q is the signed generating sum of the lattice cone modulo the central lattice, with signs fixed by kappa. For zeta primitive n-th root and eta=zeta^deg, set hat1_Q^e(lambda)=n^−1Σ_{k=1}^n zeta^(ek)hat1_Q(lambda eta^k).

Then hat1_Q^e=lambda^H∏_{alpha∈Delta_Q}(1−lambda^alpha∨)^−1; for e=−1 this is (−1)^(r−1)(∏lambda_i)/theta_Q.

items.statement: For each R∈P(M), fix the inducing character s_R explicitly. The spherical section space consists of phi on M(F)N_R(A)\G(A)/K with s_R⁻¹ phi|_M∈pi; its basis is s_R*phi_pi. Laf97 p284 and Yu p32 use s_R=rho_R (with P to be replaced by R in Yu); Yu p39 uses s_R=rho_R⁻¹. items.statement: Construct M_(R'|R)(w,lambda) by the convergent unipotent integral and meromorphic continuation on induced sections. It satisfies the composition and unitary-axis identities. Ratios M_R(lambda,P;mu)=M_(R|P)(lambda)^−1 M_(R|P)(lambda/mu) give the operator-valued (G,M)-family on its regular domain.

items.statement: For L=L_w, the map mu_w:Im X_L^G×Im X_M^L→Im X_M^G, (mu,lambda')↦lambda' mu/w^−1(lambda'), is surjective with finite kernel of size |w||X_L^L|, where |w| is the product of cycle lengths. Haar Fourier inversion converts the character sum into a normalized sum over its finite fibres.

items.name: Corrected Arthur–Lafforgue spectral expression
items.statement: For G=GL_n over F_q(X), n>0, the everywhere-unramified trace at T=0 is J_eta=Σ_[(P,pi)] |stab(P,pi)|⁻¹ Σ_[(w,tau)∈stab(P,pi)] ∫_(lambda∈A) D⁻¹ Σ_[(a,c)∈mu_w⁻¹(tau)] F_eta(lambda,a,c) d lambda. Here A=Im X_L^G, B=Im X_M^L, L=L_w, mu_w(a,c)=a*c/w⁻¹(c), D=|w||X_L^L|, and F_eta is the exact ordered regularized trace151 with h_Q(v)=hat1_Q(v eta⁻¹). Haar on A has total mass one, including all components. The finite fibre is equivalently a∈A,b∈B0,tau=a*b,c∈B,δ_w(c)=b. Replacing h_Q by hat1_Q^e gives J_e for every e∈Z. No good-representative hypothesis is required for this spectral identity. Its proof and scalar specialization require the coherent normalization and analytic prerequisites retained in S2.

items.name: Degree-zero nonvanishing of a spherical cusp form
items.statement: For a nonzero spherical vector phi in an irreducible everywhere-unramified cuspidal representation there is x∈G(A)^0 with phi(x)≠0. Use global/local Whittaker uniqueness and the spherical Whittaker value at the diagonal dictated by a canonical differential; the central degree correction has the sign forced by deg=−Σv.

items.name: A stabilizing twist fixes the spherical function
items.statement: If lambda_pi∈Fix(pi), multiplication by lambda_pi acts as the identity on A_(P,pi). First evaluate the scalar at a degree-zero nonvanishing point for cuspidal pi; extend to residual pi by the Eisenstein residue construction. On the full smooth G(A)-span it is an intertwiner, not generally the identity.

items.statement: For gcd(e,n)=1, J_e=Σ_(P,pi),w Δ_e(pi,w) B(pi,w)/(|stab(P,pi)||w||X_L^L|). Here Δ_e is the finite sum of n_pi(w,w^−1lambda_w)lambda_1^−e over lambda_pi∈Fix(pi), lambda∈X_G^G, lambda^L in the connected component with lambda_pi=lambda^L lambda and lambda_w/w^−1lambda_w=lambda^L; B is the root-basis product of N−P for n_beta on L. This is Proposition5.1.1 with its full finite-fibre conditions.

items.name: Cuspidal Rankin–Selberg degrees and poles
items.statement: For unitary everywhere-unramified cuspidal pi1,pi2 of ranks n1,n2, write L(pi1×pi2∨,z)=P/Q reduced. If they are not inertially equivalent, Q=1 and deg P=(2g−2)n1n2. In the equal case with d=|Fix(pi1)|, Q is proportional to (z^d−1)((qz)^d−1), degP=(2g−2)n1²+2d and epsilon=q^[(g−1)n1²].

items.statement: For unitary Π_i=pi_i box ν_i, ν1≥ν2, L(Π1×Π2∨,z) is the product of the shifted cuspidal L-factors over the two segments. For good representatives, N−P of L(z)/L(q^−1z) equals ν2(2g−2)n1n2, with an extra |Fix(pi1)| precisely when Π1=Π2. The arbitrary inertially-equivalent but unequal case needs an explicit twist convention.

items.statement: Write w as cycles of lengths l_j carrying Π_j=pi_j box ν_j and f_j=|Fix(pi_j)|. Set c=gcd_j(l_j f_j). The possible central lambda in Δ_e are exactly mu_c; for each such lambda, admissible stabilizing twists form a torsor under Fix(pi) intersected with the connected character torus.

items.name: Finite central character sum

items.statement: For gcd(e,n)=1 and c|n, delta_e=Σ_{d|c}mu(d)(−1)^Σ_j(l_j+l_j/(d/gcd(d,f_j))). Thus Δ_e=|X_L^L|∏_j[(−1)^(l_j−1)f_j^(l_j−1)]delta_e. The e=−1 proof separates c odd, 4|c and v2(c)=1; degree-order invariance gives the remaining coprime e.

items.name: Finite simple trees
items.statement: Reuse SimpleGraph and its IsTree predicate: a tree is connected and acyclic, equivalently it has a unique path between every pair of vertices on a nonempty vertex type. Empty vertex sets must not silently satisfy the tree convention.

items.name: Weighted graph Laplacian and tree polynomial
items.statement: For a nonempty finite vertex set and symmetric edge weights x_ij in a commutative ring, set L_ij=−x_ij off diagonal and L_ii=Σ_{j≠i}x_ij. Its row/column sums are zero. The spanning-tree polynomial is Σ_T∏_{edges(T)}x_ij, with the singleton tree contributing one.

items.name: Weighted matrix-tree theorem
items.statement: Every principal cofactor of the weighted Laplacian equals the spanning-tree polynomial. Prove the polynomial identity over Z[edge variables] by a signed determinant expansion or incidence/Cauchy–Binet argument before specializing complex weights; no positivity assumption is necessary.

items.name: Normalized first determinant coefficient
items.statement: For a singular n×n complex matrix, n≥1, define kappa(A)=([t]det(A+tI))/n. It is conjugation-invariant and equals the average of principal cofactors. The definition works for nondiagonalizable matrices and is not a pseudodeterminant based only on geometric rank.

items.name: Rank-one cofactor identities
items.statement: If A1=0, kappa(A)=det(A+1vᵀ)/(nΣv) for Σv≠0. If also 1ᵀA=0, all principal cofactors agree and kappa(A)=det(A+uvᵀ)/((Σu)(Σv)) when both sums are nonzero. Derive these by determinant multilinearity/adjugates, including rank below n−1.

items.name: Correct eigenvalue formula for kappa
items.statement: For singular complex A, kappa(A) is the product of the remaining n−1 eigenvalues divided by n after removing one zero eigenvalue, counted algebraically; it is zero if zero has algebraic multiplicity≥2. The product of nonzero eigenvalues is valid only when zero is simple. Rank n−1 alone is insufficient.

items.name: Spanning trees and type-A root bases
items.statement: The edges of the complete graph on the ordered Levi blocks correspond to roots in −Phi_Q. A set of r−1 edges is a tree iff the corresponding roots form a basis of a_L^{G,*}; cycles give linear dependencies and paths span all differences. Hence the root-basis weighted sum equals kappa of its Laplacian.

items.name: Rectangular determinant interchange
items.statement: For rectangular matrices A:m×n and B:n×m over a commutative ring with finite decidable index types, det(1−AB)=det(1−BA). This is the existing Weinstein–Aronszajn identity, used instead of a generic-diagonalizability argument.

items.name: Block compression of a determinant

items.name: Cycle-block Laplacian data

Set S_μ=Σν a_ν min(μ,ν), y_i=f_i m_i+(2g−2)d_i S_(ν_i). The positive block weights are l_i,s l_j,t[(2g−2)d_i d_j min(ν_i,ν_j)+delta_ij f_i].

items.name: Min-kernel triangularization

items.statement: Group each good discrete pair by its segment length j, obtaining a partition lambda=(j^a_j) of n. items.statement: For d|n, D_n(d)=d^−1Σ_{m|d}mu(m) C_(n/d)(X_(d/m)). A size-d orbit of geometric rank-n/d local systems induces an irreducible rank-n Weil representation with Fix of order d, not order one. Fixed points satisfy C_r(Xd)=Σ_{m|d}m O_r(m).

items.name: Arithmetic Möbius selector
items.statement: For positive t,l,L, Σ_{m≥1: ml/gcd(l,mt)|L}mu(m) is 1 if L=1 and l|t, and zero otherwise. The indexing set is finite since m≤L. Prime valuations reduce it to the divisor sum of mu over L, provided l|tL.

items.name: Representation-ring interpretation
items.statement: Restriction to the diagonal torus identifies R(GSp_2g) with Z[t±1,z_i±1]^W. Highest-weight theory gives polynomial generators t±1 and ∧^k V−t∧^(k−2)V, 1≤k≤g. The subring generated by constituents of tensor powers of V is R_g, generated by t and those fundamental expressions.
items.note: Split representation rings exist (item141), but rational algebraic GSp representations and their Weyl-character identification need a Part II of the existing classical-group roadmap.

items.name: Density and uniqueness of universal polynomials
items.statement: The Frobenius Weil tuples of genus-g smooth proper geometrically connected curves are Zariski dense in the relevant torus modulo W, in the form of Schiffmann AppendixB used by Yu. Consequently two invariant Laurent polynomials agreeing on all such curves agree identically. This is not ordinary density of arbitrary algebraic numbers.

Input to Integral universal local-system polynomial.

items.name: Rank induction and Euler-product factors
items.statement: For s<n define eta_(s,X_l)(z)=exp(Σ_{k≥1}C_s(X_(kl))z^k/k). If C_s is an integral admissible Laurent polynomial, eta is a finite quotient ∏(1−beta^l z)/∏(1−alpha^l z) with repeated monomials encoding positive and negative coefficients. Isolating C_n in item097 defines the next rational polynomial.

uses.how: Input to Independent-monomial coefficient formula.
Input to Integral universal local-system polynomial.

items.name: Independent-monomial coefficient formula
items.statement: Replace the lower-rank monomials by independent X_(i,j,s). A coefficient is zero unless Σ_{j,s}s k_(i,j,s)=a_i for every i; otherwise it is the Möbius sum of signed products binom(epsilon_(j,s)(2g−2)s S_i/l,k_(i,j,s)/l), divided by (2g−2)nΣa_i, over l dividing all k. Signs come from the binomial expansion, not the weights s.

uses.how: Input to Integral universal local-system polynomial.

items.name: Divisibility of generalized binomial coefficients
items.statement: For nonzero integer N and positive M, the integer N/gcd(N,M) divides binom(N,M), including negative upper entries. Use M binom(N,M)=N binom(N−1,M−1) and coprimality after dividing the gcd.

uses.how: Input to Primitive exponent valuation bound.
Input to Möbius-binomial integrality.

items.name: p-free factorial
items.statement: For a prime p and integer N≥0 define f_p(N)=∏_{1≤i≤N,p∤i}i=N!/[p^floor(N/p) floor(N/p)!]. It is a p-adic unit, including f_p(0)=1. Negative arguments are not admitted.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §7.2.2 p71; LZ19 equation10

uses.how: Input to Luo–Zhu p-free factorial congruence.

items.name: Luo–Zhu p-free factorial congruence
items.statement: For p odd and alpha≥1, or p=2 and alpha≥2, f_p(p^alpha N)≡f_p(p^alpha)^N mod p^(2alpha) for N≥0. Also f_2(2N)≡(−1)^floor(N/2) mod4. Pair i and p^alpha−i in the unit-residue sum and induct on N.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), §7.2.2 p71; Luo–Zhu2019 Lemma3.1, proof read

uses.how: Input to Möbius-binomial integrality.

items.name: Primitive exponent valuation bound
items.statement: In Theorem7.2.3's positive application range, with positive a_i=Σs k_(i,j,s), positive ordered nu_i, S_i=Σ_{j<i}nu_j a_j+nu_iΣ_{j≥i}a_j and positive even chi, if p does not divide gcd(k), the product χsS_i/gcd(χsS_i,k_i,j,s), over nonzero k, has valuation at least v_p(χS_mΣa). Split minimal valuations and prove both prefix and suffix inequalities.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Lemma7.2.4 pp67–70; restricted nonzero range

uses.how: Input to Möbius-binomial integrality.

items.name: Möbius-binomial integrality
items.statement: With the positive-range data of item106 and epsilon_i,j,s∈{±1}, Σ_{l|gcd(k)}mu(l)(−1)^(Σk/l)∏binom(epsilon_i,j,s χsS_i/l,k_i,j,s/l) is divisible by χS_mΣa_i. Pair l and lp; the valuation deficit 2v_p(gcd k) is cancelled by item105, with the exceptional p=2, valuation-one parity argument using chi even. Yu states more general integral nu_i and chi∈2N; zero/negative edge cases remain a gate here.

uses.how: Input to Integral universal local-system polynomial.

items.name: Integral universal local-system polynomial
items.statement: For g≥2,n≥1 there exists a unique P_g,n∈R_g such that #E_n^(F_X^k)=P_g,n(q^k,sigma_1^k,...,sigma_g^k) for every eligible curve and k≥1. Rank induction uses the bundle polynomial and item097; item107 proves integer coefficients of each partition correction and preserves the admissible monomial cone.

uses.how: Input to Top weighted term of the counting polynomial.
Input to Jacobian factor of the local-system polynomial.
Input to Low genus and low rank boundary counts.

items.name: Top weighted term of the counting polynomial
items.statement: Assign degree 2 to t and degree 1 to each z_i. For g≥2, P_g,n has unique top-weight term t^[(g−1)n²+1] with coefficient one; every other monomial has smaller weight. The leading bundle-polynomial term and strict rank-partition weight inequalities must be proved, not inferred from integrality alone.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Theorem1.1(1) p3; §7.2 with Sc16 asymptotics

items.name: Jacobian factor of the bundle polynomial
items.statement: For g≥1,n≥1, A_g,n=I_g,n J_g with J_g=∏(1−z_i)(1−t/z_i), and I_g,n is integral and has the same admissible monomial cone. Each nonempty Young diagram contains the corner factor; Adams operations preserve divisibility by J, then Gauss's lemma and the cone filtration prove integral admissible division.

uses.how: Input to Euler specialization of the bundle quotient.
Input to Jacobian factor of the local-system polynomial.

items.name: Euler specialization of the bundle quotient
items.statement: I_g,n(1,1,...,1)=mu(n)n^(2g−3). The proof imports purity of coprime Higgs moduli, Schiffmann's point-count/Poincare comparison, the nonabelian Hodge comparison with twisted character varieties, and Hausel–Rodriguez-Villegas's PGL_n Euler characteristic. These are separate substantial inputs.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Lemma7.3.1 proof p74

uses.how: Input to Euler specialization of the local-system quotient.

items.name: Jacobian factor of the local-system polynomial
items.statement: For g≥2,n≥1, P_g,n=Q_g,n J_g with Q_g,n∈R_g. The rational recurrence and induction first give divisibility over Q, then primitive-polynomial division gives integral coefficients; the cone argument keeps Q admissible. Thus #Pic^0(Xk)(F(q^k)) divides #E_n^(F_X^k).

uses.how: Input to Euler specialization of the local-system quotient.
Input to Low genus and low rank boundary counts.

items.name: Euler specialization of the local-system quotient
items.statement: For g≥2,n≥1, Q_g,n(1,...,1)=Σ_{d|n}mu(d)mu(n/d)d^(2g−3). The linear part of the trace recurrence is Σ_{d|n}C_d(X1); after division by J and evaluation at one every nonlinear term vanishes. Apply Möbius inversion to item111.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Theorem1.1(2); end§7.3 p75

items.name: Low genus and low rank boundary counts
items.statement: For n=1, Q_g,1=1 and P_g,1=J_g. For g=0 or1 and n≥2 there are no irreducible geometric rank-n local systems, so P=Q=0; this uses trivial or abelian geometric fundamental groups. The recurrence dividing by 2g−2 cannot be specialized to g=1.

items.name: Degree floor-monomial family
items.statement: Set I_Q^e=H_Q^e+s^−1(0,1,...,1). The functions lambda↦lambda^I_Q^e form a (G,M)-family, and hat1_Q^e=(−1)^dim(a_M^G)lambda^I_Q^e/theta_Q. Adjacent-block compatibility follows from the floor identities on the wall.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), LemmaA.1 p75; Laf97 Lemma5(ii)p301

uses.how: Input to Translated degree-cutoff vanishing.
Input to Dependence of cutoff values only on degree order.

items.name: Translated degree-cutoff vanishing
items.statement: For a translation-periodic (G,M)-family with compatible partial values, lim_(lambda→1)Σ_Q hat1_Q^e(lambda mu0)c_Q(lambda mu0)=0 unless mu0 is central. The auxiliary family is d_Q=hat1_Q^e(lambda mu0)theta_Q(lambda), with multiplication, not a second inverse theta.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), LemmaA.2 pp75–76, E24

uses.how: Input to Degree independence of the trace and isocline count.

items.name: Dependence of cutoff values only on degree order
items.statement: Under the same partial-value compatibility, lim_(mu→1)Σ_Qhat1_Q^e(mu)c_Q(mu) depends only on the order of e in Z/nZ. On a Levi with block sizes m_j, the top-degree floor-monomial contribution vanishes unless n|e m_j for every j; product descent gives the assertion.

uses.how: Input to Spectral reduction to finite characters and root counts.
Input to Degree independence of the trace and isocline count.

items.name: Degree-order invariance of the finite character sum
items.statement: For c=gcd(l_j f_j), c|n and a=Σl_j(l_j−1)f_j/2, delta_e depends only on ord(e mod n). Since 2a=0 mod c, a is zero or the unique element of order two. Thus e+a=0 is detected solely by whether ord(e mod c) is respectively one or two, avoiding the false lcm-of-orders assertion.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), TheoremA.4 proof p78, E26

uses.how: Input to Degree independence of the trace and isocline count.

items.name: Degree independence of the trace and isocline count
items.statement: For every n≥1 and e,e' with the same order in Z/nZ, J_e=J_e' and P_n^e=P_n^e'. Consequently the geometrically indecomposable bundle count is independent of the degree in the coprime range. Combine cutoff integrals, unitary translation invariance, and item118.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Theorem1.4; TheoremA.4 andCorollaryA.5 pp77–78

items.name: Valuation test for distinct exponential sums
items.statement: In a finite extension of Q_p (or a complete algebraically closed extension), take distinct nonzero gamma_i of positive valuation and nonzero integral c_i. Then some k≥1 has Σ c_i gamma_i^−k nonintegral. A Vandermonde system on r successive values bounds the valuations of c_i gamma_i^−k uniformly, contradicting their linear decay.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), AppendixC unnumbered lemma p81

uses.how: Input to Necessity of the admissible Laurent cone.

items.name: Ordinary curves with multiplicatively independent Weil data
items.statement: For every prime p and genus g≥1 there exists a smooth proper geometrically connected ordinary curve over some F_(p^d) such that p^d,sigma_1,...,sigma_g are multiplicatively independent. For g=1 use Honda–Tate; for g≥2 use the nonempty ordinary locus, full geometric Sp monodromy, a density-one set of mod-l monodromy groups and Chavdarov's sieve with infinitely many auxiliary primes.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), AppendixC p80; Kow06,KS99,Kob75,Ch97

uses.how: Input to Necessity of the admissible Laurent cone.

items.name: Necessity of the admissible Laurent cone
items.statement: Fix a prime p. If P∈Z[t±1,z_i±1] takes integer values on every genus-g smooth proper geometrically connected curve over finite fields of characteristic p, for all choices of paired eigenvalues, every supported monomial t^m z^u satisfies m+Σmin(u_i,0)≥0. Choose the ordinary independent curve, orient the pairs according to negative exponents and apply item120 to its constant extensions.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), TheoremC.1 pp79–81, E27

items.name: Normalizer semisimplicity input for the Weil representation argument
items.statement: If G is the reductive geometric monodromy group of the semisimple geometric restriction in §2.1, a suitable power of an element normalizing G has its semisimple part inside the group generated by G and scalar/central data as used there. Fix the exact statement of KW01 Theorem3.3(2) before implementing Yu's reduction; the unrestricted assertion for arbitrary algebraic G is not an available theorem.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Proposition2.1.3 proof p7; KW01 Theorem3.3(2)

uses.how: Input to Clifford decomposition and the twist stabilizer.

items.name: Clifford–Mackey induction across constant extensions
items.statement: For the finite-index normal inclusion W(Xd)⊂W(X1), a geometrically irreducible representation with pairwise distinct d conjugates induces irreducibly, and restriction decomposes as their direct sum. Prove continuous finite-dimensional induction, Frobenius reciprocity and the conjugacy criterion on this finite quotient; generic finite-group carrier results alone do not supply the topology.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Proposition2.1.3 proof pp7–8

uses.how: Input to Clifford decomposition and the twist stabilizer.

items.name: Serre duality for the shifted-slope argument
items.statement: For bundles U,V on a smooth projective curve, Ext1(U,V) is dual to Hom(V,U⊗omega). The actual image, saturated image, and coimage degree inequalities are needed to apply the slope bounds when the induced map is not a subbundle inclusion.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Ch15 Lemma4.2.1 proof; Yu§3.3.2

uses.how: Input to Shifted Harder–Narasimhan filtration splits.

items.name: Harder–Narasimhan existence with shifted slopes
items.statement: For an ordered real T, the T-slope function on saturated subbundles gives a unique Harder–Narasimhan filtration with T-semistable successive quotients and strictly decreasing shifted slopes. Boundedness and the maximal-slope existence proof precede the splitting result.

uses.how: Input to Shifted Harder–Narasimhan filtration splits.

items.name: Global Whittaker uniqueness and factorization
items.statement: A cuspidal GL_n automorphic representation is globally generic with multiplicity-one Whittaker functional for the chosen nontrivial additive character of A/F; its factorizable spherical vector has the restricted product of normalized local Whittaker functions. State the conductor and Haar choices rather than assuming an everywhere-conductor-zero global character.

uses.how: Input to Degree-zero nonvanishing of a spherical cusp form.
Input to Spherical Whittaker nonvanishing with conductor shift.

items.name: Spherical Whittaker nonvanishing with conductor shift
items.statement: For an unramified irreducible generic local GL_n representation, the spherical Whittaker function for a conductor-zero character is nonzero at the identity. For a character from a canonical differential of local order n_v, conjugate by diag(varpi^−(n−1)n_v,...,1) to reduce to that case.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Lemma5.3.3 proof pp37–38; Shintani76; Cogdell08 p116

uses.how: Input to Degree-zero nonvanishing of a spherical cusp form.

items.name: Cohomological tensor-duality identifications
items.statement: For lisse F1,F2 on the geometric curve, H0(F1⊗F2∨)=Hom(F2,F1), and H2(F1⊗F2∨)=Hom(F1,F2)∨(−1), Frobenius-equivariantly. Apply this to the orbit decomposition of a Weil representation to identify the self-pair H0/H2 polynomials.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Equations6.1.1–6.1.2 pp42–43, corrected E14

uses.how: Input to Cuspidal Rankin–Selberg degrees and poles.
Input to Self-pair functional equation and root radii.

items.name: Self-pair functional equation and root radii
items.statement: For a pure unitary cuspidal Weil system, the self-pair H1 has a symplectic pairing with multiplier q. Its numerator obeys P(z)=q^[(g−1)n²+d]z^[(2g−2)n²+2d]P(1/(qz)), and all roots have absolute value q^−1/2. The disjoint weights in H0,H1,H2 prevent cancellation with the denominator.

uses.how: Input to Single-cycle normalizer evaluation.

items.name: Purity and point-count polynomial for stable Higgs moduli
items.statement: For a complex smooth projective curve and coprime (n,e), the cohomology of the stable Higgs moduli is pure, and its compact-support signed Poincare polynomial is t^[2(1+(g−1)n²)] A_g,n(t²,t,...,t). The spreading/point-count comparison and cohomological convention must be supplied from Hausel05 and Schiffmann16, not assumed from smoothness.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Lemma7.3.1 proof p74; H05,Sc16 Corollary1.3

uses.how: Input to Euler specialization of the bundle quotient.

items.name: Nonabelian Hodge comparison in the twisted coprime case
items.statement: For a compact Riemann surface and coprime rank/degree, compare stable GL_n Higgs moduli with the twisted character variety with the matching central monodromy. The comparison yields the cohomological equality used for the Euler specialization; it is not an algebraic isomorphism of those moduli.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Lemma7.3.1 proof; Simpson90 input

uses.how: Input to Euler specialization of the bundle quotient.
Input to Euler characteristic of the twisted PGL_n character variety.

items.name: Euler characteristic of the twisted PGL_n character variety
items.statement: The coprime twisted PGL_n character variety of a genus-g compact surface has Euler characteristic mu(n)n^(2g−3), as HR08 Corollary1.1.1. The GL_n/Jacobian quotient and finite-group action must be matched to I_g,n; do not divide arbitrary point counts by a group order without that comparison.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Lemma7.3.1 proof; HR08 Corollary1.1.1

uses.how: Input to Euler specialization of the bundle quotient.

items.name: Ordinary locus and full symplectic monodromy of curve moduli
items.statement: In the tricanonically rigidified stable-curve moduli used by KS99 §10.6, the smooth locus is dense, the ordinary locus is nonempty open in every characteristic, and R1pi_!Q_l on the smooth universal family has geometric monodromy Sp_2g. The 3K structure is tricanonical rigidification, not an assumed prime-to-p level-three structure.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), AppendixC p80; Kob75 Theorem5; KS99 Theorems10.6.10–10.6.11

uses.how: Input to Ordinary curves with multiplicatively independent Weil data.
Input to Larsen–Chavdarov maximal Weyl-group specialization input.

items.name: Larsen–Chavdarov maximal Weyl-group specialization input
items.statement: For the universal curve family with full symplectic geometric monodromy, establish a density-one set of primes l with full mod-l Sp image, then the density of fibres whose zeta numerator has full Weyl Galois group. Yu uses Chavdarov's proof with infinitely many auxiliary primes instead of its printed almost-all hypothesis; this weakening needs a checked proof-level adapter.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), AppendixC p80; Kow06 Proposition3; Ch97 Theorem2.1

uses.how: Input to Ordinary curves with multiplicatively independent Weil data.
Input to Ordinary maximal-Weyl eigenvalue independence.

items.name: Ordinary maximal-Weyl eigenvalue independence
items.statement: For an ordinary curve with irreducible zeta numerator and full S_g⋉(S2)^g Galois group, a selected reciprocal half of the eigenvalues together with q is multiplicatively independent. The p-adic slopes are 0 and v_p(q); changing the chosen half permits any prescribed pattern of these valuations.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), AppendixC; Kow06 Proposition1 proof andLemmas1–2

uses.how: Input to Ordinary curves with multiplicatively independent Weil data.

items.name: Genus-one ordinary existence for the cone test
items.statement: For every prime p, the polynomial X²+X+p is an ordinary elliptic Weil polynomial and Honda–Tate realizes it by an elliptic curve over Fp. Its paired roots and p provide the multiplicative independence needed by item121.

uses.how: Input to Ordinary curves with multiplicatively independent Weil data.

items.name: Stack mass and rational stable Higgs objects
items.statement: For a finite groupoid define its mass as Σ_[x]1/|Aut(x)|. In the coprime stable Higgs case, show the rational-point/coarse-object comparison and scalar automorphism group before using mass=#Higgs^st(Fq)/(q−1). This is the precise conversion in AppendixB.

uses.how: Input to Higgs count and geometrically indecomposable bundles.

items.name: Explicit rank-two and rank-three recurrence checks
items.statement: For g≠1 and coprime degrees, P_1=C1; P_2=C2+(g−1)C1²+C1; P_3=C3+4(g−1)C1C2+(g−1)C1 C1(X2)+2(g−1)²C1³+2(g−1)C1²+C1. These are coefficient identities extracted from the same formal recurrence, not independent numerical assumptions.

items.name: Vandermonde determinant and invertibility criterion
items.statement: For a finite vector v over a commutative ring, det(vandermonde v)=∏_i ∏_(j>i)(v_j−v_i). In an integral domain this determinant is nonzero exactly when v is injective. Over a field this makes the consecutive-power system invertible.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), AppendixC proof input; pinned Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Vandermonde.lean:219,233

uses.how: Input to Valuation test for distinct exponential sums.

items.name: Split representation ring and character map
items.statement: For a field k and monoid G, TauCeti.repRing k G is SplitK0(FDRep k G), with direct-sum relations and tensor multiplication. Its ring character map sends [V] to character(V). This is not automatically the exact Grothendieck ring or the ring of rational algebraic representations of GSp.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5 (18 July 2022), Remark7.1.1 input; pinned RepresentationRing/Basic.lean:106–142

uses.how: Input to Representation-ring interpretation.

items.name: Haar probability preserved by a surjective homomorphism
items.statement: A continuous surjective homomorphism f:G→*H, with H a compact topological group, Borel measurable spaces and Haar measures of equal total mass, is measure preserving. Use probability Haar on all compact character groups, including disconnected ones.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5, §§5.2.2–5.2.3 pp32–36; detailed derivation in the continuation report

uses.how: Input to Normalized transfer along a finite compact-group cover.

items.name: Pointwise Fourier inversion on a finite dimensional torus
items.statement: For a finite index type d and f:C(UnitAddTorus d,C), summability of mFourierCoeff f implies HasSum (n↦mFourierCoeff f n • mFourier n x) (f x) at every x. The L² expansion alone does not give point evaluation.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5, §§5.2.2–5.2.3 pp32–36; detailed derivation in the continuation report

uses.how: Input to Pointwise character inversion gives the fibre average.
Input to Smooth Fourier decay on the character groups in the trace formula.

items.name: Normalized finite character orthogonality
items.statement: For a finite additive group G and an additive character ψ with values in a characteristic-zero semifield, its normalized expectation is one for the trivial character and zero otherwise. Apply to complex characters of finite cyclic component groups and Z/nZ, n>0.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5, §§5.2.2–5.2.3 pp32–36; detailed derivation in the continuation report

uses.how: Input to Pointwise character inversion gives the fibre average.
Input to Smooth Fourier decay on the character groups in the trace formula.
Input to Degree Fourier recovery of the spectral contribution.

items.name: Cycle coordinates for the spectral character cover
items.statement: Let w permute equal-rank blocks of M. Index its nonempty cycles by j, with length l_j≥1 and common block rank d_j≥1; N_j=l_j*d_j and n=ΣN_j. In unit-circle coordinates z_(j,t), define T by ∏_(j,t)z_(j,t)^d_j=1; A consists of cycle-constant u_j with ∏u_j^N_j=1; B satisfies ∏_t v_(j,t)^d_j=1 separately for each j, and B0 satisfies ∏_t v_(j,t)=1 separately. Embed A and B in T. These are respectively Im X_M^G, Im X_L^G, Im X_M^L and its identity component, L=L_w.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5, §§5.2.2–5.2.3 pp32–36; detailed derivation in the continuation report

uses.how: Input to Finite-kernel torus Fourier inversion.
Input to Difference map on every Weyl cycle.
Input to Degree and fibres of the spectral cover.
Input to Typed finite-fibre operator trace.

items.name: Difference map on every Weyl cycle
items.statement: For the groups in145, δ_w:B→B0, v↦v/w⁻¹(v), is surjective, with kernel ∏_j μ_(N_j). Every fibre has ∏_j N_j points, even when B is disconnected.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5, §§5.2.2–5.2.3 pp32–36; detailed derivation in the continuation report

uses.how: Input to Finite-kernel torus Fourier inversion.
Input to Degree and fibres of the spectral cover.

items.name: Degree and fibres of the spectral cover
items.statement: The continuous homomorphism mu_w:A×B→T, (a,c)↦a*δ_w(c), is onto with |ker mu_w|=D=(∏l_j)(∏N_j)=|w|*|X_L^L|. For any tau∈T its fibre consists of the finite pairs a∈A, b∈B0 with tau=a*b, followed by c∈B with δ_w(c)=b. There are ∏l_j outer pairs and ∏N_j inner lifts.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5, §§5.2.2–5.2.3 pp32–36; detailed derivation in the continuation report

uses.how: Input to Finite-kernel torus Fourier inversion.
Input to Pointwise character inversion gives the fibre average.
Input to Typed finite-fibre operator trace.

items.name: Normalized transfer along a finite compact-group cover
items.statement: For a continuous surjective homomorphism p:H→K of compact abelian Lie groups with finite kernel F of size D>0, define Tr_p f(y)=D⁻¹Σ_(p(x)=y) f(x). For continuous f this is continuous, and for smooth f it is smooth. Every group carries probability Haar.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5, §§5.2.2–5.2.3 pp32–36; detailed derivation in the continuation report

uses.how: Input to Finite-kernel torus Fourier inversion.
Input to Pointwise character inversion gives the fibre average.

items.name: Pointwise character inversion gives the fibre average
items.statement: For p:H→K as in148 and smooth complex f on H, at every y∈K the absolutely convergent character sum Σ_(χ∈Khat) ∫_H χ(p(x)/y)*f(x) dx equals Tr_p f(y). Equivalently the coefficient indexed by χ is the (χ⁻¹)-Fourier coefficient of Tr_p f. Apply p=mu_w and y=lambda_pi to obtain (5.2.12) with factor D⁻¹.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5, §§5.2.2–5.2.3 pp32–36; detailed derivation in the continuation report

uses.how: Input to Finite-kernel torus Fourier inversion.

items.name: Smooth Fourier decay on the character groups in the trace formula
items.statement: On a finite product of Circle and a finite abelian group, a smooth complex function has absolutely summable Fourier coefficients. For torus dimension d and integer s with 2s>d, |fhat(k)|≤C(1+4π²||k||²)^(-s). The statement includes dimension zero and is uniform in a compact auxiliary parameter when the corresponding derivatives are uniformly bounded.
items.locator: Yu arXiv:1807.04659v5, §§5.2.2–5.2.3 pp32–36; detailed derivation in the continuation report

uses.how: Input to Pointwise character inversion gives the fibre average.

items.name: Typed finite-fibre operator trace
items.statement: For a discrete pair (P,pi), (w,tau)∈stab(P,pi), L=L_w, a∈A, b∈B0, tau=a*b and c∈B with δ_w(c)=b, put z=lambda*c for lambda∈A. Define R_Q(z;v)=M_(R|P)(z)⁻¹∘M_(R|P)(z/v), where R∈P^Q(M), v∈X_L^G. For h_Q=hat1_Q(·eta⁻¹) or hat1_Q^e, set F_h(lambda,a,c)=lim_(mu→1 in X_L^G) Tr_(A_P,pi)[(Σ_(Q∈P(L))h_Q(mu*a) R_Q(z;mu*a))∘M(w,w⁻¹(c))∘U_tau]. U_tau is multiplication by tau. The Q-sum is continued holomorphically before evaluation at mu=1; the other parameters are unitary.

items.name: Degree Fourier recovery of the spectral contribution
items.statement: Let n>0, zeta primitive of order n and eta=zeta^deg. If J_(eta^k)=Σ_(e mod n)zeta^(ek) J_e, then J_e=n⁻¹Σ_(k mod n)zeta^(−ek)J_(eta^k). In151 this replaces hat1_Q(mu*a*eta^(−k)) by hat1_Q^e(mu*a)=n⁻¹Σ_k zeta^(ek)hat1_Q(mu*a*eta^k), leaving the fibre, operator order and denominator unchanged. It holds for every integer e, not just coprime e.
